clue.text: Gave out second message of approval, performed outside

indicators.note: the word for performed is placed around the other pieces, so they sit outside them

parts.note: performed means did
a tribute is a message or statement of praise and approval

explanation.surface: Someone handed things out after a second word of praise, all done in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out goods or leaflets is to share them among people, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Go off course entering Belgrade via Tehran

indicators.note: the answer is entering, or found within, the run of letters Belgrade via Tehran

explanation.surface: A traveller strays from the planned route by going into Belgrade by way of Tehran.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from a set path or norm is the core sense of this verb; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Outburst from Sarah getting very old

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: An elderly woman named Sarah has a sudden tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley of shots, and by extension a sudden burst of words or criticism, is a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Cider-drinking girl on street looking most embarrassed?

parts.note: Rosie of Cider with Rosie, Laurie Lee's memoir, in which the girl shares cider with the young author

explanation.surface: A girl who has had too much cider, out on the street, is red-faced with shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's well-known memoir of an English village childhood. The question mark admits the definition is indirect: blushing makes a face rosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment brings a blush, so the pinkest-cheeked person looks most abashed; a playful, indirect definition.

clue.text: Plot involving devious chat in groups

indicators.note: involving means the garden-plot word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed

indicators.note: devious means the letters of chat take a crooked, rearranged route

explanation.surface: Conspirators hatch a scheme with sly talk in small cliques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a conspiracy, but it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Items sorted and handled in lots or sets are arranged into clusters; a direct equivalent.

clue.text: Momentary crying about politician getting nothing right

indicators.note: about means the word for crying goes around the other pieces

parts.note: teary means tearful, crying
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A brief fit of weeping over an MP who keeps getting everything wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting only a moment and lasting only a while are near synonyms: both mean short-lived.

clue.text: I'd upset member of the upper class, not half — I've put something on record

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters of I'd are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the noble's word is kept

parts.note: an aristocrat is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to upsetting a toff, but only partly, and admits having noted it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person by the answer: a keeper of a journal could say this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps a daily journal records events in writing, so could claim this.

clue.text: Rebels, unruly lot corralled by ministers of religion

indicators.note: corralled by means penned inside the clergy word, like cattle in an enclosure

parts.note: Revs, short for Reverends, are clergymen

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of lot are out of order

explanation.surface: A disorderly band of insurgents is rounded up by the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel and to rise up against authority are the same verb in third-person form.

clue.text: Get home for a bun!

parts.note: a bun is a bunny, so a home for one is the wooden pen a pet rabbit lives in; 'Get' reads as an instruction to acquire it

explanation.surface: An order to pop home for a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bun' reads as a bakery item, but it is short for bunny.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden cage a pet bunny lives in is literally its house, a whimsical description.

clue.text: Male pets? Mum collects 100 to be held by kids

indicators.note: to be held by means the inner group sits inside the word for kids

parts.note: tots are small children

indicators.note: collects means the word for mum takes the hundred inside it

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A mother gathers a hundred pets for her children to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Male felines are toms, and cats are common household pets; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Keeps disappearing at the seaside?

parts.note: keeps are castle towers; the ones built on the beach vanish when the tide comes in

explanation.surface: Something at the coast that keeps vanishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a verb meaning 'continues', but it is a noun: strongholds.
explanation.definitionFit: Children build little forts on the beach that the incoming tide washes away; a cryptic description.

clue.text: One bit of veg, nothing beside? Hardly this then!

definitions.text: One bit of veg, nothing beside? Hardly this then!

indicators.note: beside means the zero is placed next to the vegetable

parts.note: a bean is a single item of vegetable
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A meal of one bean and nothing else is no feast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a single bean with nothing alongside would hardly be a jolly party.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy celebration or party is the British informal meaning, the very opposite of a meagre plate.

clue.text: Haiti open possibly for native far from there

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of Haiti open may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Haiti might open its doors to a person from a distant land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Haiti: the native comes from a country in Africa, a long way from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in an East African country is a native of a land far from the Caribbean.

clue.text: Bill provided in island clothes shop is not accurate

indicators.note: in means the bill sits inside the island-and-shop pair

parts.note: Next is a British high-street clothing retailer
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A receipt from a clothing store on an island turns out to be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: NEXT is a chain of clothes shops found in most British towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise and inaccurate are synonyms; the definition's 'is' is absorbed as the adjective describes the state.

clue.text: Hate to lessen — love taking minutes to enter

indicators.note: to enter means the love-and-minutes group goes into the word for lessen

parts.note: to abate is to lessen or diminish

indicators.note: taking means the zero takes the minutes alongside it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
MIN is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: A plea to reduce hatred, with love given time to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something intensely is a straight synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Radical doctor heading off cold — something fizzy to be swallowed

indicators.note: to be swallowed means the fizzy drink goes inside the doctor-and-cold pair

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor; heading off just places it ahead of the cold
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A bold doctor tackles a cold by prescribing a fizzy remedy to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' reads as 'warding off' the cold, but only says the doctor goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme or far-reaching measures are both described this way; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Drink brought round in the morning, given to male in bed

indicators.note: brought round means the wine word encircles the other pieces

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A man is served a drink in bed first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' simply joins AM and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging bed of canvas or netting slung between supports is a specific kind of bed.

clue.text: Resent unchangeable outlook

parts.note: to mind something is to object to or resent it
set means fixed, unchangeable

explanation.surface: Someone resents a rigid, fixed way of seeing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual attitude or way of thinking is a person's view on the world; a synonym.

clue.text: Relations, good first and last, given honour in country

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: first and last means only the outside letters of good are taken

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Family members, well behaved throughout, are decorated by the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British award given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a monarch is a nation or state, so a country.

clue.text: Checks hovels, stifling expression of surprise when knocked over

indicators.note: stifling means the pigsty word smothers the other piece inside it

parts.note: sties are filthy hovels, pigpens

indicators.note: knocked over means the exclamation is upended and read backwards

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An inspector examines slums, suppressing a gasp when bowled over.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart or obstruct someone is to block their progress; a verb synonym.

clue.text: She's beginning to head off to keep appointment and calms down

indicators.note: to keep means the shortened word holds the appointment inside
off means that letter is taken away from she's
beginning to means only the first letter of head is used

parts.note: a date is an arranged appointment

explanation.surface: A woman sets off for a meeting, which soothes her nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'S loses H, the start of 'head', to leave SES, which holds DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tranquillise someone, often with a drug, is to soothe or quieten them; a synonym.

clue.text: Extreme cold here in Normandy on headland

parts.note: ici is French for here, and Normandy is in France
a ness is a headland or promontory, as in Loch Ness place names

explanation.surface: It is bitterly cold here on a Normandy cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Frostiness and bitter chill are the same quality; the noun names the state of being frozen.

clue.text: Under strain, nurse is interrupted by awful noise

indicators.note: interrupted by means the anagram breaks into the middle of the nursing word

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

indicators.note: awful means the letters of noise are in a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: A nurse's work is disrupted by a terrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched taut or put under stress has been tightened; the past participle fits.

clue.text: Child unwell — having this?

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A poorly youngster: could it be a cold?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: an unwell child may well be suffering this.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish shiver or mild cold is a common ailment of a sick youngster.

clue.text: Goods in vehicle on journey

indicators.note: on means the journey word comes after the vehicle in this down entry

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a go is a trip or turn, a journey

explanation.surface: Merchandise carried in a van on its trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight carried by ship, plane or lorry is the load of merchandise; a synonym.

clue.text: Partner to manage thriftily

definitions.meaning: a man married to someone is their spouse, their life partner
as a verb, to use resources sparingly, as in conserving one's strength

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a married man; the verb means to conserve resources carefully, an old farming sense.

clue.text: Sailor acquires objects for shooting practice

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
gets means acquires

explanation.surface: A seaman picks up some things to shoot at.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards or marks aimed at by archers and riflemen are what one practises shooting on.

clue.text: This tremor's destroyed electronic devices

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of this tremor's are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An earthquake's shaking has wrecked the gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistors whose resistance varies with temperature are components used in circuits, so electronic parts.
